title: Basic Merge Conflict
objective: Resolve a two-branch, one-file merge conflict so that both branches' changes to the same line are preserved in the final result.
description: You will create two branches that edit the same line of a shared file differently, then merge them to trigger your first conflict. Your job is to read the conflict markers, combine both edits, and complete the merge commit. This is the fundamental workflow you will repeat in every real-world conflict.
hints: Run the merge and study the output carefully; Git tells you exactly which file is in conflict before you open anything.
Open the conflicted file and locate the <<<<<<<, =======, and >>>>>>> markers; each side of the marker block is one branch's version of the line.
Edit the file to keep both changes in a sensible order, remove all three marker lines, then git add the file and commit to finish the merge.
